scenes.tts: Two nuclei, each dotted with bright spots of a glowing protein. Is a spot a droplet of that protein? Or is it a cluster of binding sites, such as many copies of one DNA sequence? Under a microscope, the two can look alike.

scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). Two large cutaway nuclei side by side, each a soft GREY-outlined circle about 70% of frame height, centred at x = -3.3 and x = +3.3. Inside both, about 40 small BLUE dots (the protein) drift slowly for the whole film. COLOUR MAP for the whole film: BLUE = protein molecules; TEAL = droplets, the dense phase; ORANGE = binding sites and parking spaces; YELLOW = the saturation concentration; PURPLE = DNA and chromatin (hook and last scene only); GREY = outlines, dial, gauges, axes; white = words. Small corner label on the nuclei: 'schematic'. Opening frame: each nucleus shows five identical soft white-blue glows (the microscope view), the label 'what the microscope sees' above them and a large white '?' between the nuclei. On 'a droplet of that protein', the LEFT glows sharpen into TEAL filled discs packed with blue dots, label 'droplets'. On 'binding sites', the RIGHT glows sharpen into small fixed clusters of short ORANGE bars with blue dots sitting on them, label 'binding sites'. On 'DNA sequence', each ORANGE cluster is shown sitting on a short faint PURPLE strand (repeated copies of one sequence), which fades again with the blur. On 'look alike', both sides blur back into identical glows; the two labels stay small above each nucleus.
Title 'Bigger or Brighter?' fades in across the top for 2 s over the same world; blue dots keep drifting and the glows pulse gently. The '?' between the nuclei fades out.

scenes.tts: A nucleus has no membrane-bound compartments inside it, yet it holds many bodies like these. The largest, the nucleolus, builds ribosomal subunits. Many of their molecules carry several weak sticky patches, so each can hold many partners at once. That is multivalency.

scenes.visual: Same two nuclei. On 'no membrane-bound compartments', a dashed GREY ring flickers around one glow in each nucleus and dissolves: no wall. On 'the nucleolus', a larger soft grey blob fades in low in each nucleus, labelled once 'nucleolus' between the nuclei with two thin leader lines; a tiny grey particle labelled 'ribosomal subunit' drifts out of the left nucleolus toward the nuclear edge. On 'sticky patches', a round magnifier inset grows out of one left glow into the centre of the frame: one BLUE rounded blob with four small white patches on its rim; three neighbour BLUE blobs dock at three of the patches, each link a short wobbling white line. Label 'weak sticky patches'. On 'multivalency', that word appears under the inset while links break and re-form. The inset shrinks back into its glow as the scene ends.

scenes.tts: The usual checks cannot tell droplets from sites. Both kinds of spot look round. Droplets fuse, and site clusters can drift together until they look merged. Bleach one with a laser, and it glows again, because molecules that bind and let go refill it too. A bright spot shows only that the protein is concentrated there.

scenes.visual: Both nuclei in microscope view (identical glows). A row of three GREY labels slides in along the bottom: 'round', 'merge?', 'refills'. On 'look round', every spot in both nuclei pulses and a white tick appears under 'round' for each nucleus. On 'Droplets fuse', in the LEFT nucleus two neighbouring glows touch, merge and relax into one round glow. On 'look merged', in the RIGHT nucleus two glows drift together until their blurs overlap into one; a small cutaway bubble shows the ORANGE bars underneath are still two separate clusters, side by side. Tick 'merge?' on both sides, the right tick drawn with a '?'. On 'Bleach one', a white flash darkens one spot in each nucleus and both regain their glow over about 3 s at visibly different, unmatched paces (schematic: only the occurrence of recovery is a claim); two small cutaway bubbles show why: left, blue dots swapping across a TEAL droplet edge; right, blue dots hopping off and onto ORANGE bars. Tick 'refills'. On 'concentrated there', the ticks fade and a white caption reads 'concentrated, but how?'.

scenes.tts: So change the amount instead. Give both nuclei one dial: the total protein, averaged over the whole nucleus. Add a gauge that reads the concentration outside the spots. Now double the protein in both. What will each outside gauge do?

scenes.visual: The check row slides away. A large GREY dial rises into the top centre between the nuclei, labelled 'total protein', pointer at 30% of its range (no numbers). Under each nucleus a horizontal GREY gauge with a white needle appears, labelled 'outside'. Show each, then name it. Both needles sit at the same height (computed: at this setting both models give the same outside value). On 'double the protein', a faint ghost pointer appears on the dial at 60% of its range; the real pointer does not move yet. On 'What will each outside gauge do?', a question card appears top centre: 'Double it. What do the gauges do?'
Predict pause, 4.5 s. The question card 'Double it. What do the gauges do?' stays on screen. Near-stillness by design: blue dots drift slowly, both needles blink gently, the ghost pointer pulses.

scenes.tts: The droplet needle holds still. Think of salt water past saturation: added salt stops dissolving and forms a second phase. At equilibrium under fixed conditions, one protein on its own holds the outside at the saturation concentration. The extra builds more of a second, denser phase: the droplets. They take up more room, but glow no brighter. Bigger, not brighter.

scenes.visual: The question card fades; the dial pointer sweeps to the ghost position over 3 s. Both sides change together, but the RIGHT side is dimmed to 40% so the eye stays left. LEFT: the needle stays exactly still; a YELLOW tick appears on the gauge under it, labelled 'saturation concentration'. The TEAL droplets swell so that their TOTAL area grows about 2.5-fold (computed from the lesson's made-up phase model, saturation 1 and dense phase 50, total 3 to 6: dense-phase fraction 4.1% to 10.2%; no numbers on screen); droplet number stays the same and their colour strength never changes. Schematic: only the total TEAL area is a claim, not how it is split among droplets. On 'denser phase', the label 'dense phase' appears on one droplet for 2 s. On 'salt water', a small inset at upper left: a beaker with salt grains falling in, a 'dissolved' bar beside it staying flat while a white crystal pile grows at the bottom; label 'saturated salt water'. The inset fades on 'At equilibrium'. On 'Bigger, not brighter', the TEAL words 'bigger, not brighter' appear under the left nucleus and stay for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: On the site side, the needle climbs. Think of the sites as parking spaces, a fixed number, with plenty still free. Some protein is parked and the rest is outside, so the outside rises with the total. The spots fill in and glow brighter, but grow no bigger. Brighter, not bigger.

scenes.visual: The LEFT side dims to 40%, keeping its label; the RIGHT lights. A small rewind icon flashes over the right nucleus, its state rewinds, then replays while a ghost copy of the dial pointer sweeps again. The right needle climbs steadily (computed from the made-up sites model in scene s09; outside rises to three times its start). The ORANGE clusters keep exactly the same size while more blue dots land on their bars, so each glows brighter. On 'parking spaces', an inset at upper right: a grey parking lot with 8 ORANGE-outlined spaces; BLUE cars arrive, park and leave; about half the spaces are taken at first and more as cars arrive, while more cars also drive on the street. Label 'parking spaces'. On 'Brighter, not bigger', the ORANGE words 'brighter, not bigger' appear under the right nucleus and stay.

Silent hold, 3.5 s. Both sides lit, side by side: left needle on its YELLOW tick, right needle well above it; the labels 'bigger, not brighter' (TEAL) and 'brighter, not bigger' (ORANGE). Dots drift, droplets shimmer, the parking inset fades out.

scenes.tts: Keep turning. On the site side, the parking lot fills up. The spots brighten more slowly, and nearly every extra molecule stays outside, so that needle climbs faster. Within this range, the droplets keep taking up more room, and their needle stays put.

scenes.visual: Each gauge transforms into a graph below its nucleus: the gauge bar rotates to become the vertical axis 'outside', and a horizontal axis 'total protein' grows from its foot (no numbers on either axis). The nuclei shrink into the top half and keep changing. The dial spins back to zero and sweeps steadily to its maximum over the scene; each needle tip leaves a trace. LEFT graph (computed: phase model, saturation 1, dense phase 50, total 0 to 10, made-up units): no droplets while the trace rises at 45 degrees; it meets a dashed YELLOW line 'saturation concentration' with no droplet yet, the first visible droplet appears just after, and then the trace runs flat along the yellow line while the total TEAL area keeps growing (computed: dense-phase fraction reaches 9/49, about 18%, at the dial's maximum; no numbers on screen). RIGHT graph (computed: one kind of site, binding capacity 4 and dissociation constant 1 in the same units): the trace rises with a shallow slope, then bends up toward a thin dashed GREY guide labelled 'outside = total' as the ORANGE clusters reach full brightness; a small ORANGE badge 'nearly full' lights on the clusters. Corner label on each graph: 'made-up model, computed'.

scenes.tts: So here is the test, in its simplest form. Add more protein, and watch where the extra goes. At equilibrium under fixed conditions, one protein forming a phase puts it into more droplet volume, outside held still. A fixed set of sites puts it onto those sites: brighter spots, until they are full.

scenes.visual: Graphs and nuclei stay. Between them, centred, white text builds: 'Where does the extra go?'. On 'more droplet volume', a TEAL arrow runs from that text to the left droplets with the words 'more volume'; the total TEAL area grows slightly once more. On 'onto those sites', an ORANGE arrow runs to the right clusters with 'fixed sites: brighter'. On 'until they are full', the ORANGE 'nearly full' badge pulses.

scenes.tts: This clean version is for one protein that separates on its own. Real bodies hold many kinds of molecule, some may form on chromatin, and tiny spots blur size into brightness. So where the extra goes is a clue, not a proof. The text below shows what each complication changes.

scenes.visual: Arrows fade. A white tag 'one protein, on its own' appears over the left nucleus. Then three white tags slide in, one per clause, each with a small change to the world: 'many kinds of molecule' (a pale second colour appears as a ring inside one TEAL droplet); 'on chromatin' (a short PURPLE strand appears and one droplet settles onto it); 'tiny spots' (one spot shrinks into a soft blur in which size and brightness cannot be told apart). On 'a clue, not a proof', the white words 'a clue, not a proof' appear centred for the rest of the scene. On 'The text below', the tags dim and drift toward the bottom edge.
End card, 4.5 s. The world dims behind. Centred, large, in white: 'Where extra protein goes is a clue to how a spot formed.' with 'clue' emphasised. The droplets keep shimmering faintly behind.
